# Outline — THE CONDITION REPORT

## Structure

- **Form:** novel. 38 chapters, ~83,600 words, chapter target 2,200.
- **POV:** dual first person, present tense, alternating. Chapters 1–23:
  odd = Lena, even = Sebastiaan. **Chapter 26 breaks the alternation** —
  chapters 25 and 26 are both Lena's, because his point of view is not
  available for the eleven days at the depot. From chapter 27 the parity is
  permanently flipped: odd = Sebastiaan, even = Lena.
- **Beat system:** Romancing the Beat, dark register. Four phases, not acts.
- **Span:** nineteen weeks, Monday 8 January to Thursday 21 May.

### The four phases and their marks

| Phase | Chapters | % | Beats |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Setup** | 1–4 | 0–10.5% | Both leads in separate lives with separate goals; the No Way / Adhesion at the end of ch 4 |
| **2. Falling in Love** | 5–19 | 10.5–50% | Inkling of Desire (ch 6), Deepening Desire (ch 10, 12), Maybe This Could Work (ch 14, 18), Midpoint of Love (ch 19) |
| **3. Retreating from Love** | 20–28 | 50–73.7% | Inkling of Doubt (ch 20), Deepening Doubt (ch 21–22), Retreating (ch 23–25), Shields Up (ch 26–28) |
| **4. Fighting for Love** | 29–38 | 73.7–100% | Break Up / Black Moment (ch 29–30), Dark Night of the Soul (ch 31–32), Grand Gesture / Relinquishment (ch 33), resolution and HFN (ch 34–38) |

### Themes

**The central question: is there any repair that is not also a forgery?**

Both leads make losses invisible for a living and both call it care. He
restores property to families and takes a third of it. She fills a tear so
well that no one can find it. The book has no position on this and refuses
to acquire one; it puts a woman who hides damage next to a man who hides
damage and lets the reader watch what happens when the damage is a person.

Secondary threads: what a signature is worth in a system that cannot
unfile anything; whether protecting someone against their stated wish is
care or theft; the difference between a thing being over and a thing being
corrected.

### MICE threads

- **M (Milieu — the trade and the house at Kloosterstraat).** Opens ch 1,
  closes ch 38. Outermost tag.
- **I (Inquiry — is the Schindler-Wolff Zurich claim honest, and whose hand
  is on the paper?).** Opens ch 4, closes ch 37 with the tribunal ruling and
  the amended Zurich file.
- **E (Event — the forged filing disrupts Lena's professional existence).**
  Opens ch 5, closes ch 34 when the referral against B-4471 is withdrawn and
  she has a new, worse equilibrium.
- **C (Character — Sebastiaan's dissatisfaction with being the current
  instalment of a fraud).** Opens ch 8, closes ch 33 with the corrigendum.

Nested and closed in reverse: C (33) → E (34) → I (37) → M (38).

# PHASE 1 — SETUP (ch 1–4, 0–10.5%)

### Ch 1: "Raking Light" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **POV/mode:** Lena, first person present.
- **Location:** Academy conservation studio and Studio 4B, Mutsaardstraat;
  her flat, Lange Riddersstraat. Monday 8 January.
- **Beat:** Setup — the constrained lead's separate life and separate goal.
- **% mark:** 0–2.6%
- **Emotional arc:** absorbed → thwarted
- **Try-fail:** No, but — the fellowship application is short one thing (a
  letter of institutional support), but the board does not meet until June.
- **Beats:**
  1. Lena working the Van der Weyden underdrawing fragment under raking
     light. Fifteen minutes of pure procedure, establishing her hands, her
     competence, her age (thirty-three, ten years on the register, B-4471
     read aloud off a form), and her divorce as a fact she mentions the way
     she mentions the humidity.
  2. Studio 4B: the nineteen keys, the kettle, the standing faculty minute
     barring Corvelijn & Zonen from the premises since 2019. She likes this
     room because of what cannot come into it.
  3. She warms her right hand in her left sleeve. The old scaphoid break,
     the bicycle, the cobbles at nineteen.
  4. Fellowship deadline 1 June; she needs paid work between now and then
     and the Academy cannot give her any. A letter from Corvelijn & Zonen
     offering four months of condition work at more than she has ever been
     paid.
  5. Berchem: Armand's flat, tools on the wall, bench cleared. She does not
     tell him whose letter it is. He asks anyway and she lies about the
     name, badly.
- **Plants:** the wrist; the nineteen keys and the standing bar; B-4471 as a
  public number; the 1 June deadline; her ability to *make* materials, shown
  as craft when she mixes her own wheat starch paste rather than buying it;
  the tuition question she has never asked her father.
- **Payoffs:** none (opening).
- **Character movement:** she takes a job she knows the shape of and takes
  it anyway, for the fellowship. First choice of the book, made freely.
- **The lie:** reinforced. She fills a loss on the fragment so well that her
  supervisor cannot find it, and is praised, and it makes her ill.
- **Opening image:** her hands steady under a lamp at three times
  magnification. (Mirrored in ch 38.)

### Ch 2: "Carrying Cost" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** Kloosterstraat 118; a call to Basel. Tuesday 9 January.
- **Beat:** Setup — the darker lead's separate life and separate goal.
- **% mark:** 2.6–5.3%
- **Emotional arc:** controlled → pressed
- **Try-fail:** No, and — the Zurich counterparty rejects the firm's
  condition evidence as unsigned by a registered conservator, *and* the
  March reckoning is eleven weeks out.
- **Beats:**
  1. Sebastiaan works a claim file at seven in the morning. Establishes
     him: forty-one, divorced 2018, nine years in the chair, will not sit
     down in his own house.
  2. The claim book, physically — calfskin, hand-updated since 1951 —
     against the index, eleven drawers of private research. He explains the
     difference to a junior and the junior does not understand it. Nobody
     ever does.
  3. Telephone call with Ruth Schindler-Wolff, 88, in Basel. He is kind to
     her, at length and without performance, and it is the most likeable he
     will be for twenty chapters.
  4. The Zurich counterparty's letter: the condition evidence must be
     signed by a conservator on the Belgian register or the claim does not
     advance. He has no such conservator. He hires one.
  5. €4.1m; 31 March; three misses and the Vier appoint an administrator;
     he has missed one.
- **Plants:** claim book vs index; clause 9 glimpsed on the framed deed he
  does not read; the Faller matter mentioned as a nine-year joke; Ruth's
  existence and her age; his want, stated flat and independent of Lena.
- **Character movement:** he decides to hire Lena Brassart specifically, off
  a register search, and the reader sees exactly why.
- **The lie:** stated for the first time, to the junior, as procedure: "The
  docket does not remove. It appends."

### Ch 3: "Fifty-one Per Cent" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the white room, third floor, Kloosterstraat. Monday 15 Jan.
- **Beat:** Setup — the two leads in a room; the working relationship.
- **% mark:** 5.3–7.9%
- **Emotional arc:** wary → engaged
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — the work is the best she has ever been given, but
  the terms of engagement include a confidentiality undertaking she signs
  without a lawyer.
- **Beats:**
  1. The white room: north light, 50% RH, the dehumidifier's hum, the hot
     tap that has never worked. She is given a key. He stands in the
     doorway with his coat on and does not come in.
  2. The 1913 Feininger with the tidemark and the 1960s bleaching. The
     exemplar exchange: "Tell me what you would do." "Nothing, for six days."
  3. She writes and signs a genuine condition report on a genuine object.
     The reader watches what her signature costs her to give, and what it
     means: registration number, date, the formula "in my opinion and on
     inspection".
  4. She notices he prints his name in block capitals on a scrap before he
     signs anything.
  5. Kasimir Ott delivers a crate and looks at her the way a man looks at a
     load he will later have to move.
- **Plants:** the block-capital tell; the dehumidifier hum as a house alarm;
  the confidentiality undertaking; the white room key; Kasimir's assessment.
- **Payoffs:** the Feininger (planted ch 2 as the claim's second object).
- **Character movement:** she gives him a real signature, freely, once. This
  is the only one she ever gives.
- **The lie:** reinforced — she proposes a sympathetic fill on the tidemark
  and he approves it without asking whether it should be visible.

### Ch 4: "Eleven Seconds a Page" — Sebastiaan, 2,600 words
- **Location:** his kitchen; the front office scanner. Thursday 18 January.
- **Beat:** **THE NO WAY / ADHESION.** The imposed adhesion, on the page.
- **% mark:** 7.9–10.5%
- **Emotional arc:** deliberate → satisfied → sleepless
- **Try-fail:** Yes, and — he gets the filing through *and* Bram Six gets it
  same-day date-stamped, which is worse for everyone.
- **Beats:**
  1. Zurich's deadline. He drafts a forty-page condition report on the
     Schindler-Wolff drawing containing a finding Lena has not made and
     would not make: that the 1948 Basel restoration is consistent with the
     family's account of continuous possession.
  2. The kitchen table, the Rotring, her staff card propped against the
     salt, four attempts. Registration number B-4471 copied from the public
     register, which he did not even have to steal.
  3. He lets the moment before the upload run its full length on purpose,
     so that afterwards he can say he took it. Then presses the key.
  4. He calls Bram Six from a phone box on the Vlaamsekaai and pays for a
     same-day stamp — which forecloses the three-week window in which Lena
     could have caught it in the queue. This is the specific act that makes
     the rest of the book possible.
  5. He does not sleep. He counts what it is worth: €38–44m of claim book,
     eleven weeks, one signature.
- **Plants:** B-4471 on a filed document; Bram Six; the phone box; the
  Basel 1948 restoration as a contested fact.
- **Payoffs:** the block-capital tell (ch 3) — he prints her name, not his.
- **Character movement:** the Lie is now operational rather than
  philosophical. He has spent someone else's signature.
- **Adhesion mechanism, stated:** Article 11. From this date nothing can be
  removed from the docket. She has no exit that does not run through a
  confession.

# PHASE 2 — FALLING IN LOVE (ch 5–19, 10.5–50%)

### Ch 5: "Append-Only" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the white room; Rue de la Loi, Brussels. Monday 22 January.
- **Beat:** the constrained lead learns the machinery.
- **% mark:** 10.5–13.2%
- **Emotional arc:** routine → detonation → cold clarity
- **Try-fail:** No, and — she cannot get it withdrawn, *and* the attempt
  puts her on Rachida Bekkali's radar as the report's author.
- **Beats:**
  1. A courtesy copy of the filed report arrives for her records. Page
     thirty-one. "That's my number. That's not my hand."
  2. She takes the 08:41 to Brussels without telling him. Rachida Bekkali,
     registry counter, Article 11 explained flatly: the docket appends, it
     does not remove. A correction is possible. A removal is not.
  3. Rachida asks the question she already knows the answer to — "Did you
     sign this, Ms Brassart?" — and Lena does not answer it, and both of them
     understand exactly what the non-answer is.
  4. Back at Kloosterstraat, the confrontation. He does not deny it, does
     not apologise, and produces the 1997 Armand Brassart report from the
     drawer without being asked, laying it on the table like a valuation.
  5. Article 19 explained: a fraud finding reopens twenty-two restitutions,
     nine of them already sold. The leverage is not a man. It is
     twenty-two households and her father inside them.
- **Plants:** Article 11 and the corrigendum mechanism named in passing by
  Rachida; Article 19; the 1997 report as a physical object with a paperclip
  rust-mark; Rachida's unanswered question.
- **Payoffs:** B-4471 (ch 1, ch 4); Bram Six's same-day stamp (ch 4) — she
  learns she was three weeks too late by four days.
- **Character movement:** she stays. Not from fear — from arithmetic she has
  chosen to accept as hers.
- **The lie:** challenged for the first time. Her invisible-repair ethic is
  the exact thing he has used against her: a document nobody can see the
  join in.

### Ch 6: "Doorframe" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the house, top to bottom; the third-floor landing. Wed 24 Jan.
- **Beat:** **Inkling of Desire.**
- **% mark:** 13.2–15.8%
- **Emotional arc:** managerial → unsettled
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — she agrees to keep working, but sets no terms
  yet, and her compliance frightens him more than a refusal would.
- **Beats:**
  1. Practical arrangements: she works Monday to Thursday in the white
     room, he does not go in. The doorframe habit begins.
  2. He watches her lift a sheet with a slip of Japanese tissue and a
     brush, and the chapter's desire is entirely about attention — his, to
     her hands, and hers, to an object that cannot consent either.
  3. Dinner is not offered. He has never offered anyone anything; he
     describes the circumstances under which food would exist and she has to
     step into them, and does, and hates that she does.
  4. The alarm code, 1109. He tells her because he needs her to be able to
     leave the building at night, and the reader is told what the number is
     and not why.
  5. Dries Neefs telephones the office about the 2019 story, unprompted,
     and is stonewalled. Sebastiaan makes a note of the date.
- **Plants:** 1109; the doorframe; Dries Neefs and the killed 2019 piece;
  the dehumidifier cutting out when the landing door is held.
- **Character movement:** he begins wanting a thing he has no procedure for.
- **The lie:** reinforced — he tells himself the filing is now simply part
  of the record, and therefore no longer an act.

### Ch 7: "Two Meetings on Credit" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** Vervoort's chambers, Brussels; a train. Friday 26 January.
- **Beat:** exits tested and priced.
- **% mark:** 15.8–18.4%
- **Emotional arc:** hopeful → costed out
- **Try-fail:** No, but — no affordable legal route, but she learns the one
  mechanism that will matter in eighty pages.
- **Beats:**
  1. Griet Vervoort walks her through every exit and prices each one: the
     suspension of B-4471 (eleven months minimum), the criminal route
     (standing lies with the heirs, not her), the press (a second breach
     stacked on the first).
  2. **The corrigendum.** Vervoort, almost in passing: "Any signatory to
     the original may file one. At any time. Without leave. Including him."
     Lena writes it down. The reader must feel this land and then let it go.
  3. Retainer €6,000. Lena has €2,340. Vervoort gives her two meetings on
     credit and is honest about the fact that she will then stop.
  4. She tells Souad on the phone from the train. Souad tells her to leave
     Antwerp and take the Rotterdam bench.
  5. She does not go home. She goes to Studio 4B and sits in the dark with
     the presses.
- **Plants:** the corrigendum, explicitly, in dialogue, at 17%; Vervoort's
  credit limit; the Rotterdam bindery.
- **Payoffs:** Article 11 (ch 5); the standing bar on the firm (ch 1) — 4B
  is the one room he cannot enter.
- **Character movement:** she now knows the shape of the whole machine,
  including its one door, and cannot afford to use any of it.

### Ch 8: "A Splice Takes Four Times As Long" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** Vandewiele's yard, Deurne; the depot. Tuesday 30 January.
- **Beat:** what the darker lead is subject to, dramatized.
- **% mark:** 18.4–21.1%
- **Emotional arc:** confident → measured → cornered
- **Try-fail:** No, and — Emiel will not move the 31 March reckoning, *and*
  the audit right under clause 22 is read aloud.
- **Beats:**
  1. Emiel Vandewiele in a cordage yard that smells of tar and new rope.
     One question, then an uncomfortable wait. The splice-versus-knot line.
  2. The pledge: €4.1m, the claim book as collateral, one miss recorded,
     two more and an administrator. Clause 22: **any public allegation of
     professional misconduct triggers an immediate audit right.**
  3. Emiel mentions his cardiologist once, without weight, and moves on.
  4. The Faller matter comes up as the yard's standing joke — nine years in
     a Zurich tribunal, the firm a third-party claimant, "it will outlive
     all of us and then it will outlive the lawyers."
  5. Kasimir at the depot afterwards: the broken thermostat, the freight
     lift, the empty camera housings from the 2014 system that was never
     wired. Kasimir states his four rules, including seventy-two hours.
- **Plants:** clause 22; Emiel's heart; the Faller matter and its timetable;
  the thermostat; the empty camera housings; Kasimir's four rules; the
  second schedule Emiel refers to and will not show.
- **Character movement:** the March deadline becomes a countdown the reader
  can do arithmetic on.
- **The lie:** untouched — this chapter is where the reader learns that his
  Lie is expensive to maintain, not merely convenient.

### Ch 9: "No" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the white room. Wednesday 31 January.
- **Beat:** **the constrained lead's first refusal, and it stands.**
- **% mark:** 21.1–23.7%
- **Emotional arc:** braced → immovable
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — she refuses and the refusal holds, but she now
  has to live inside a house where she has just won.
- **Beats:**
  1. He needs the second document: a signed report on the 1913 Feininger
     dating the 1948 Basel restoration. Genuine signature this time, because
     Zurich's lawyers will now check the hand against the first.
  2. He describes the circumstances under which she would sign it. She
     says no. Not about the price — "because it isn't true and I'd have to
     look at it under a lamp for the rest of my life."
  3. He does not override her. He cannot: a second forged signature on the
     same claim is the one thing the counterparty's lab will catch. Her
     refusal is not moral leverage, it is **structural** leverage, and she
     realises this mid-scene and goes quiet with it.
  4. He leaves the room and does not slam anything. The dehumidifier
     resumes.
  5. She writes the true condition report instead — the one that says the
     1948 restoration is inconsistent with continuous possession — and
     leaves it on the table unsigned, which is both a gift and a threat.
- **Plants:** the unsigned true report, left in the white room, which
  becomes an object in ch 22 and again in ch 33.
- **Payoffs:** the Feininger (ch 3); Zurich's signature requirement (ch 2).
- **Character movement:** the balance moves toward her for the first time,
  at 23.7%, and the cause is an act, not a mood.
- **The lie:** challenged — she has just declined to make something
  invisible.

### Ch 10: "Nothing" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the office; the Sint-Andries quarter at night. Friday 2 Feb.
- **Beat:** **Deepening Desire**, in the negative.
- **% mark:** 23.7–26.3%
- **Emotional arc:** furious → recalculating → something worse
- **Try-fail:** No, and — the claim stalls eleven weeks *and* he solves the
  wrong problem.
- **Beats:**
  1. He does the arithmetic of overriding her: forge the second signature,
     lose the lab test, lose the claim, lose the book. He does **nothing.**
     The ledger records it and it is the most consequential nothing in the
     first half.
  2. Instead he removes the obstacle he *can* remove. Tomas Beke has filed a
     competing research note on the Schindler-Wolff drawing's 1948
     whereabouts. Sebastiaan tells Kasimir to make Beke unavailable.
  3. Kasimir's methods, stated: an inventory card from the Antwerp city
     archive, a flat, an anonymous call. Nothing that leaves a mark.
     Sebastiaan says "do it" out loud, on the page, in one syllable.
  4. He walks home past her building and does not go up, and the reader is
     given the full interior of a man deciding not to, which is the desire
     beat.
  5. Kasimir's exercise book: the ledger of favours, going back to 2003.
- **Plants:** the inventory card; Kasimir's exercise book; the word "do it".
- **Payoffs:** her refusal (ch 9) — he cannot override it, and the reader
  watches him fail to.
- **Character movement:** he redirects cruelty from the person who refused
  him to a person who cannot refuse him. This is the pattern the whole book
  turns on and it is stated here for the first time.

### Ch 11: "The Card in the Flat" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the Academy; Beke's flat door; Kloosterstraat. Tue 6 Feb.
- **Beat:** the constrained lead sees the machinery operate on a third party.
- **% mark:** 26.3–28.9%
- **Emotional arc:** unease → recognition → complicity
- **Try-fail:** No, and — she cannot help Beke *and* she discovers she is
  connected to his ruin from years back.
- **Beats:**
  1. Tomas Beke arrested. The archive accreditation is suspended the same
     morning, administratively, which does not wait for a court.
  2. Lena recommended Beke for the 2019 Academy loan that got the firm
     barred from the premises. Her one safe room exists because of him.
  3. She goes to his flat. His partner will not open the door past the
     chain. Somebody has already told them who she works for.
  4. She asks Sebastiaan directly, in the office, in front of two staff.
     He does not deny it. He prices it: "He was going to cost us the
     January window, which is about nine months and eight hundred thousand."
  5. She goes to 4B and cannot work.
- **Plants:** Beke's partner; the 2019 loan as the origin of the bar.
- **Payoffs:** the inventory card (ch 10); the standing bar (ch 1, ch 7).
- **Character movement:** her constraint acquires a second floor — she is
  not only held, she is now standing on someone.
- **Narrative stance note:** the harm registers in Beke's partner's refusal
  to open a door and in Lena being unable to work for two days. No narration
  tells the reader anything.

### Ch 12: "Four Boxes" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the cellar; the office; the framed deed. Friday 9 February.
- **Beat:** Deepening Desire; the darker lead's interior opened.
- **% mark:** 28.9–31.6%
- **Emotional arc:** restless → exposed
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — he finds the clause that will save him, and does
  not understand yet that it is a door rather than a wall.
- **Beats:**
  1. He takes the 1974 deed out of its frame for the first time in nine
     years and reads it properly. Clause 9, in full: a steward may resign by
     transferring the book into the escrow of a competent public authority,
     and the personal liability transfers with it. He reads it twice and
     puts it back in the frame.
  2. Clause 14: the index is personal property, written that way by Jozef
     in 1974 to keep research away from creditors. He has always known this
     and has never said it aloud to anyone.
  3. The cellar door, the four boxes with the years in grease pencil, two of
     the years wrong. He does not open them. He has never opened them.
  4. Lena works late. He stands in the doorframe and they talk for forty
     minutes about foxing, and it is the closest thing to intimacy either
     of them has had in years, and he does not come into the room.
  5. She asks what his father was like. He gives her a valuation instead of
     an answer, and hears himself do it.
- **Plants:** clause 9 in full; clause 14 in full; the four boxes; the
  grease-pencil years.
- **Character movement:** he now knows there is an exit from the stewardship
  and files it away as unthinkable.
- **The lie:** reinforced — he tells her, in the doorframe, that a document
  is only a lie if someone withdraws it, and she says "that's not what a lie
  is", and he does not answer.

### Ch 13: "Three Things" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the office; the yard behind Kloosterstraat. Mon 12 February.
- **Beat:** **the bargain whose terms she sets.**
- **% mark:** 31.6–34.2%
- **Emotional arc:** decided → hard → nearly satisfied
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — she gets all three terms, and one of them is
  honoured with an object that is not what she thinks it is.
- **Beats:**
  1. She names terms, unprompted, before he asks for anything: the 1997
     report in this room today; no door she cannot open from the inside;
     and if her number goes on anything again she walks into Rue de la Loi
     and takes her father with her.
  2. He agrees to all three, aloud, which is the first agreement in the
     book and therefore the first thing that can be breached.
  3. In exchange she will complete the Zurich condition work — the
     *genuine* parts, the physical examination and the materials analysis —
     and will sign nothing.
  4. Berchem, that evening. Armand's line: "You are keeping a chair warm
     for a man who would rather stand. Let them have me, Lenneke." He asks
     her to stop protecting him. She refuses. **The leverage does not want to
     be leverage and she overrules him**, which makes her captivity partly
     her own construction and she knows it.
  5. The yard, dusk, a galvanised bucket. He brings out a folder and she
     burns it and watches until it is ash.
- **Plants:** the three terms as a spoken agreement; the bucket; Armand's
  request, refused.
- **Payoffs:** the 1997 report (ch 5); the leverage mechanism (ch 5).
- **Character movement:** she converts a hold into a contract, which is the
  first move of the balance toward level.
- **The lie:** challenged from an unexpected side — Armand tells her that
  making his ruin invisible is not care.

### Ch 14: "A Laser Print" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the yard; his office; the strongroom. Monday 12 Feb, later.
- **Beat:** **Maybe This Could Work**, undercut in the same chapter.
- **% mark:** 34.2–36.8%
- **Emotional arc:** something like happiness → the old reflex
- **Try-fail:** Yes, and — he keeps the leverage *and* gets the intimacy,
  which is the worst possible outcome for his arc.
- **Beats:**
  1. The burn, from his side. He watches her face while a laser print of the
     1997 report goes up in a bucket. The original is in the strongroom, in a
     sleeve, with a rust-mark from a paperclip on the top left corner.
  2. He does not decide to deceive her. He simply does not do the other
     thing, and the chapter is honest about the difference being nothing.
  3. Afterwards: the kitchen, an actual meal, his contractions coming back,
     four-word sentences. He tells her about the Pechstein in the Ghent
     sacristy and is delighted and twenty-five years younger.
  4. He almost tells her about the boxes. Stops.
  5. Strongroom, midnight. He photographs the original and puts it back.
- **Plants:** the paperclip rust-mark on the original — the physical detail
  that will convict him in ch 20.
- **Payoffs:** the bucket (ch 13); the block-capital signature habit (ch 3).
- **Character movement:** he acquires something to lose and immediately
  insures against losing it, in the only way he knows.

### Ch 15: "Nineteen Keys" — Lena, 1,800 words — **QUIET CHAPTER**
- **Location:** Studio 4B; Souad's bindery, Sint-Andries. Sat 17 February.
- **Beat:** breathing room; the Want under pressure.
- **% mark:** 36.8–39.5%
- **Emotional arc:** tired → briefly whole → frightened
- **Try-fail:** No, but — the fellowship slips out of reach, but she gets one
  clean afternoon of her own work.
- **Beats:**
  1. Four hours on the Van der Weyden fragment, uninterrupted. Pure
     procedure and pure pleasure. The best writing in the first half.
  2. Her supervisor: at this rate the treatment will not be published by 1
     June and the board meets once. She does not tell him why she is behind.
  3. Souad's bindery: linen thread, wheat paste, a spine being oversewn.
     Souad's argument, first full statement — leave, take the Rotterdam
     bench, let Armand fall.
  4. Lena cannot answer it and knows she cannot, and drinks tea instead.
  5. Walking home she checks over her shoulder for the first time in her
     life and is angry with herself for it.
- **Plants:** the Rotterdam bindery bench, named, offered; the 1 June board
  meeting as a single event.
- **Payoffs:** the fellowship Want (ch 1) begins visibly dying.

### Ch 16: "Probate" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the yard; a restaurant on the Leopold de Waelplaats. Tue 20 Feb.
- **Beat:** the structure tightens; the successor arrives.
- **% mark:** 39.5–42.1%
- **Emotional arc:** managing → outflanked

- **Beats:**
  1. **Hanne Vandewiele**, 46, insolvency lawyer, at her father's shoulder

     across the table as an observation about liability, not a suggestion.
  2. Emiel, tired, mentions the cardiologist a second time and is
     irritated at himself for mentioning it.
  3. Emiel privately: "Your father borrowed nine hundred thousand from me on
     a handshake in 1991 and paid it back early." He does not say the rest.
  4. Meike, Sebastiaan's ex-wife, at the next table with someone else. Two
     minutes of conversation, entirely without rancour, in which she says

  5. He goes back to the office at eleven and works until four.
- **Plants:** Hanne as the person who understands the deed; the 1991
  handshake; Emiel's heart, second mention.
- **Payoffs:** clause 9 (ch 12) — reinforced by a second character, from

### Ch 17: "Iron Gall" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** Studio 4B, overnight; the white room. Thursday 22 February.
- **Beat:** **the hidden capability, deployed.**
- **% mark:** 42.1–44.7%
- **Emotional arc:** cornered → focused → appalled and exhilarated
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — she makes a weapon, but it is a weapon shaped to
  fit her own hand into a cell.
- **Beats:**
  1. She has read the whole Zurich file now and she knows the claim is
     dishonest: the 1948 Basel restoration cannot be reconciled with
     continuous possession, and Ruth Schindler-Wolff is going to be handed a
     picture on a false record.
  2. She cannot expose it — the exposure runs through B-4471, through the
     Commission, through Armand.
  3. So she manufactures a contradiction instead. Overnight in 4B, with
     nineteen keys' worth of privacy and a room the firm cannot enter: a
     1953 Basel loan receipt on period stock, iron-gall ink of the right
     recipe, aged, foxed, with a chain-line and watermark that will pass.
     It states that the drawing was on loan in Basel in 1953, which cannot
     be true if the 1948 restoration is what the firm says it is.
  4. She seeds it into the Zurich annex file in the white room, where it
     will be found by anyone who audits, and where **only a conservator can
     tell it is wrong** — which means she controls the detonator.
  5. She washes her hands for a long time and says nothing to anyone. Not
     Souad. Not Armand.
- **Plants:** the 1953 receipt as a physical object; the word **Basel**
  attached to it; the fact that she can do this at all.
- **Payoffs:** her materials capability (ch 1, shown as craft); Article 19
  (ch 5) — she now understands the whole machine well enough to build a part
  for it.
- **Character movement:** she stops being held and starts being armed. The
  balance begins moving toward her a second time.
- **The lie:** at its absolute deepest. She has made an invisible repair to
  a document, on purpose, and told herself it is honesty.

### Ch 18: "Something in the Annex" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the white room doorway; the office. Friday 23 February.
- **Beat:** **Maybe This Could Work**, second statement.
- **% mark:** 44.7–47.4%
- **Emotional arc:** warm → briefly suspicious → warm
- **Try-fail:** No, but — he does not find the receipt, but he registers
  that something in the room has changed and misreads it as her softening.
- **Beats:**
  1. He touches the annex file and does not open it. Two inches from it.
  2. Kasimir warns him: "You've got a conservator with a key and a grudge
     and a set of hands, and that's the trouble with —" and does not finish.
     Sebastiaan dismisses it.
  3. He tells her about the day he was nineteen — not the lamp, not yet;
     the version where his father was simply impressive.
  4. She asks him what he would do if the Zurich claim were dishonest. He
     answers as a professional and it is a genuinely good answer and it is
     also the answer of a man who has never once withdrawn anything.
  5. He does not come into the room. Again.
- **Plants:** Kasimir's unfinished warning, which is correct.
- **Payoffs:** the doorframe (ch 6) — nine weeks of not crossing it.

### Ch 19: "Basel" — Lena, 2,600 words
- **Location:** the white room; the third-floor landing. Monday 26 February.
- **Beat:** **MIDPOINT OF LOVE.** The negotiated scene, on the page.
- **% mark:** 47.4–50.0%
- **Emotional arc:** taut → deliberate → altered
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — they get what they both want, and each of them
  now has something to lose that is not the other's compliance.
- **Beats:**
  1. The negotiation is explicit, unhurried, and takes three pages before
     anything happens. What is on the table, what is not, what she will not
     be asked, what he is not permitted to assume. Both of them are better
     at this than at conversation because it is a specification.
  2. **The word that ends it is "Basel."** She chooses it. He does not ask
     why she chose it and the reader knows exactly why and this is the most
     dangerous sentence in the book.
  3. He crosses the doorframe for the first time in six weeks. Her
     interiority does not stop, not for a paragraph — she is aware of the
     latch, of the hygrometer, of her wrist, of what she has hidden four feet
     away in the annex file.
  4. Afterwards, on the landing, both of them say plainly what it was. This
     is the confirmation the contract requires and it is written to be
     good, not dutiful.
  5. What each now stands to lose, stated in interiority on both sides
     across the chapter break: she can go to prison for the receipt; he can
     be refused by someone whose compliance he already owns.
- **Plants:** "Basel" as a spoken word with two meanings.
- **Payoffs:** the doorframe (ch 6, 12, 18); the dehumidifier hum (ch 3, 6).
- **Character movement:** midpoint reversal — both leads shift from reactive
  to active, and the balance is level for the first and only time.

# PHASE 3 — RETREATING FROM LOVE (ch 20–28, 50–73.7%)

### Ch 20: "Rust-Mark" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the strongroom; the kitchen. Wednesday 28 February.
- **Beat:** **Inkling of Doubt** — hers, watched from inside him.
- **% mark:** 50.0–52.6%
- **Emotional arc:** open → caught → accurate
- **Try-fail:** No, and — he is caught *and* his defence makes it worse.
- **Beats:**
  1. She has been in the strongroom, legitimately, for a crate. The 1997
     report is in a sleeve with a rust-mark from a paperclip on the top left
     corner. The thing she burned had no rust-mark. Laser toner sits on the
     surface; iron-gall ink does not. She knew within four seconds.
  2. The confrontation, from his POV, which is the correct choice: the
     reader watches him fail to say the true thing while narrating his own
     failure with total accuracy. **He becomes more precise as he lies** —
     dates, page numbers, sums — and she names the tell out loud.
  3. He does not offer the original now. He explains why keeping it is
     rational. It is rational.
  4. She does not shout, does not leave, and goes back up to the white room
     and works, and he stands at the bottom of the stairs.
  5. The first breach of the ch 13 agreement is not one of the three terms.
     It is the thing underneath them.
- **Payoffs:** the rust-mark (ch 14); the accuracy tell (ch 3, ch 12); the
  bucket (ch 13).
- **Character movement:** he loses her belief and keeps his collateral,
  which is the exchange rate he has used his whole life.

### Ch 21: "Twenty-two Families" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the flat; Souad's bindery. Saturday 2 March.
- **Beat:** **Deepening Doubt.**
- **% mark:** 52.6–55.3%
- **Emotional arc:** flat → argued with → resolved
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — she starts building a file, but building it
  requires the confidentiality breach Vervoort warned about.
- **Beats:**
  1. She begins assembling a document set: the filed report, the courtesy
     copy, the register entry, the dates. Everything with a stamp on it.
  2. **The reader learns her second secret** — 2009, the Munch drawing, the
     second time, which she has never told Rachida and which means her own
     hands are not clean when she walks in.
  3. Souad, at full force: "Twenty-two families is not your arithmetic. You
     didn't sign it. You're carrying a bill somebody else ran up because
     carrying it is the only way you get to keep him."
  4. Lena says out loud, for the first time, that she does not want to leave,
     and that this is not the same as wanting to stay.
  5. She writes Dries Neefs's name on the back of a tram ticket and does not
     call him for nine days.
- **Plants:** the tram ticket; the nine days.
- **Payoffs:** the press exit (ch 7); Souad's position (ch 15).
- **The lie:** she is now conscious of it and still choosing it.

### Ch 22: "Preliminary Docket" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the office; a phone box; Ekeren. Monday 4 March.
- **Beat:** **the retreat's cause — he does the thing he has always done.**
- **% mark:** 55.3–57.9%
- **Emotional arc:** pressured → decisive → hollow
- **Try-fail:** Yes, and — the pressure works on Zurich *and* it costs him
  the only thing he had.
- **Beats:**
  1. Zurich stalls. Twenty-seven days to the reckoning. He needs the
     counterparty to settle rather than test the file.
  2. He lodges a two-page summary of the 1997 Armand Brassart report on the
     Commission's **preliminary** docket — the informal shelf, not a formal
     allegation, visible to counterparties and to nobody else. It is a
     signal to Zurich that he is willing to burn a conservator.
  3. It is not one of the three terms. It is the spirit of all three. He
     knows this while doing it and does it in eleven minutes.
  4. Same afternoon: the Ekeren vehicle completes on Lena's building. He
     did not initiate it this week; he initiated it in January and it lands
     now, and he does not stop it, which is not the same as doing it and is
     also not different.
  5. Bram Six calls: someone at the registry has pulled the preliminary
     entry. Sebastiaan assumes Zurich. It is Rachida.
- **Plants:** the Ekeren vehicle; Rachida pulling the entry.
- **Payoffs:** the 1997 report (ch 5, 13, 14, 20); clause 22 (ch 8) is now

- **Character movement:** the retreat is caused by him being exactly what he

### Ch 23: "Date-Stamps" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** a café on the Ossenmarkt; the flat. 11–12 March.
- **Beat:** **Retreating** — the escape that half works.
- **% mark:** 57.9–60.5%
- **Emotional arc:** cold → committed → sick
- **Try-fail:** Yes, and — it publishes *and* it fires clause 22.
- **Beats:**
  1. She learns about the preliminary docket entry from Armand, who was

  2. Dries Neefs, café, ninety minutes. He is not her friend and says so.
     He takes a partial file: the report, the register entry, the stamps.
     She holds back the 1997 material entirely, to protect Armand, which
     means the story is half a story.
  3. She gives him nothing about the Zurich claim's dishonesty because that

  4. **12 March, 06:00.** *De Wacht* publishes: a firm filing conservators'

     conservator who "declines to confirm authorship".
  5. By 09:30 clause 22 has fired and the Vier's audit is instructed. Lena
     understands within the hour that she has handed the file to the exact
     people who will now go through the annex.
- **Payoffs:** Dries (ch 6, 7, 21); clause 22 (ch 8); the tram ticket (ch 21).
- **Character movement:** her largest independent action, and it produces a

### Ch 24: "Instructed" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the yard; the office; a corridor. Wednesday 14 March.

### Ch 25: "Nine Minutes in Fifty" — Lena, 2,600 words — **POV BREAK BEGINS**
- **Location:** the Deurne depot. Thursday 15 March – Saturday 24 March.
- **Beat:** Retreating; the physical constraint, once, at full weight.
- **% mark:** 63.2–65.8%
- **Emotional arc:** disbelief → procedure → attrition
- **Try-fail:** No, and — every attempt fails *and* the failures cost her
  body.
- **Beats:**
  1. Taken from the white room at ten in the morning, walked to a van by
     the upper arms. Nothing that leaves a mark a hospital would ask about,
     except that it does, for eleven days.
  2. The depot as a physical system, learned: nine minutes of heat in
     fifty, the roller door's three stages, the freight lift's folding gate,
     the empty camera housings, soup at seven and seven.
  3. She acts, repeatedly, and none of it works and all of it is action:
     she moves terracotta pallets twice a day to keep the body from
     negotiating; she works out the lift's interlock and gets as far as the
     yard on day six and is walked back; she writes the entire Zurich
     argument on the back of a delivery manifest in pencil, from memory,
     because it is the only thing she owns.
  4. Kasimir, twice a day, keeping a receipt for the camp bed. His rule of
     seventy-two hours passes on day four and he does not release her,
     because in twenty-one years he has never acted without an instruction.
  5. The cold reaches the old scaphoid break on day two and the ulnar numbness
     starts on day seven and by day nine she cannot hold a pencil for more
     than four minutes.
- **Payoffs:** the wrist (ch 1); the thermostat, the housings, Kasimir's
  rules (ch 8); the freight lift (ch 8).
- **Character movement:** the injury that ends one kind of work forever
  begins here, on a specific day, for a specific reason.
- **Narrative stance:** the harm registers entirely in her body and her
  procedure. No narration comments. Not once.

### Ch 26: "Day Eleven" — Lena, 2,200 words — **POV BREAK; PARITY FLIPS AFTER**
- **Location:** the depot; the van; Kloosterstraat. Monday 25 March.

  3. He learned on 18 March, day three. She works this out from a

  4. She goes to her own flat, which he owns, and puts a chair against the

  5. Ruth Schindler-Wolff's letter is on the mat — forwarded by the firm,

### Ch 28: "Two Microns" — Lena, 1,800 words — **QUIET / AFTERMATH CHAPTER**
- **Location:** a hand clinic, Antwerpen-Zuid; the white room. Wed 4 April.
- **Beat:** **Shields Up**, completed. Aftermath, not escalation.
- **% mark:** 71.1–73.7%
- **Emotional arc:** numb → diagnosed → plain
- **Try-fail:** No, and — the tremor is permanent *and* she has to say it

  1. Nine days late to a doctor. The bruising is yellow and the

  2. Diagnosis: ulnar compression numbness, resolving; a fine tremor at
     high magnification, not resolving. Invisible infill under a stereo
     microscope is finished. Everything else — lining, pressing, visible

  3. She goes to the white room, puts her hand flat on the table, picks up a

     times and that's the only place it's ever mattered."

### Ch 29: "Chain Lines" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words

  2. **Sebastiaan learns Lena can forge**, from an auditor, in a kitchen,

### Ch 31: "Grease Pencil" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the cellar; Rue de la Loi. Wednesday 18 April.

### Ch 32: "Visible Repair" — Lena, 1,800 words — **QUIET CHAPTER**
- **Location:** the Rotterdam bindery. Tuesday 24 April.
- **Beat:** her Dark Night, and her decision.
- **% mark:** 81.6–84.2%
- **Emotional arc:** flat → working → decided

     it will reach him. He says, "Good."
- **Payoffs:** the fills (ch 1, 3, 15); Rotterdam (ch 15, 21, 30); Armand's
  request (ch 13).
- **Character movement:** the Lie breaks. She chooses the visible repair.
  Note that this happens **before** anything he does, and is not caused by
  him.

### Ch 33: "Corrigendum" — Sebastiaan, 2,600 words
- **Location:** Kloosterstraat; Rue de la Loi registry. Tuesday 5 May.
- **Beat:** **THE GRAND GESTURE — the relinquishment.**
- **% mark:** 84.2–86.8%
- **Emotional arc:** resolved → exposed → light
- **Try-fail:** Yes, and — he ends the hold *and* it costs him everything he
  has been holding.
- **Beats:**
  1. Morning: he drafts the corrigendum to the Zurich condition report. The
     operative sentence is one line long and states that the signature of
     H. Brassart, B-4471, on the filing of 18 January was made by
     Sebastiaan Corvelijn. He signs it **without printing his name on a
     scrap first**, and the signature is visibly not his usual one.
  2. Same document, second instrument: a clause 9 resignation as
     *bewindvoerder*, transferring the claim book into the escrow of the
     Commission. Sixty live claims. He carries it to Brussels himself in a
     document case, on a train, at 13:40.
  3. **Registry counter, 15:40**, twenty minutes before the registry closes
     at four. Rachida takes it, reads the first paragraph, and stops
     reading, and looks up. She acts within four hours: the referral against
     B-4471 is withdrawn the same evening because the *parket* has no case
     against a signatory who did not sign, and a fresh referral is opened
     against him.
  4. Lena is standing in the corridor at Rue de la Loi with her own two
     pages when he comes out, because she came to file her account of the
     1953 receipt and neither of them knew the other would be there. She
     files hers. Neither of them speaks. **This is the only time in the book
     they are in the same building and do not speak.**
  5. **Friday 8 May: Emiel Vandewiele dies in his kitchen at 74.** Reported
     at the chapter's end in four lines, three days after the filing, and
     it has nothing to do with anything anyone did.
- **Payoffs:** the corrigendum (ch 7, 31); clause 9 (ch 12, 16); Article 11
  (ch 5); the block-capital signature tell (ch 3, 4, 14); Emiel's
  cardiologist (ch 8, 16).
- **Character movement:** the Need beats the Want. He withdraws something.
  It is the first subtraction of his life.
- **The hold ends here, by his decision, on 5 May, three days before the
  death.** That order is fixed and is the spine of the resolution.

### Ch 34: "Withdrawn" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** Rotterdam; Berchem. Friday 8 May.
- **Beat:** free, and undecided.
- **% mark:** 86.8–89.5%
- **Emotional arc:** disbelieving → free → unresolved
- **Try-fail:** Yes, but — she is legally clear, but nothing she lost comes
  back.
- **Beats:**
  1. Vervoort telephones, unpaid, because she wants to: the referral is
     withdrawn, B-4471 is clean, her own filed account has been accepted as
     a voluntary disclosure and drawn a reprimand, not a suspension.
  2. **What does not come back:** the Academy fellowship (the board met on 2
     May and the Van der Weyden treatment was not published); the tremor;
     Tomas Beke's accreditation; the twenty-two families' exposure, which is
     unchanged because Article 19 is still Article 19.
  3. Berchem. Armand, told everything. The negotiation: he will not walk
     into Rue de la Loi, on the condition that she stops treating him as a
     thing to be protected. It is the least sentimental scene in the book
     and neither of them cries.
  4. He tells her, flatly, that Lucien Corvelijn paid her third-year
     tuition in 2013. He does not explain it. Nobody in this book explains
     it.
  5. End of chapter: Souad, from Antwerp, with the news that Emiel
     Vandewiele died this morning.
- **Payoffs:** the fellowship (ch 1, 15, 28); the tuition (ch 1); Beke (ch
  11); Armand's want (ch 13).
- **Character movement:** free to go anywhere, with a permanent injury, a
  reprimand, and no fellowship. The equilibrium is new and it is worse, and
  it is hers.
- **MICE:** E-thread closes.

### Ch 35: "Off the Door" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** Kloosterstraat; the depot. Monday 11 – Thursday 14 May.
- **Beat:** the consequences arrive, and are absorbed.
- **% mark:** 89.5–92.1%
- **Emotional arc:** braced → stripped → oddly rested
- **Try-fail:** No, but — he is barred, but the barring removes a weight he
  never chose.
- **Beats:**
  1. **The Commission's decision, 14 May:** Sebastiaan Corvelijn is struck
     from the register of recognised representatives for five years. He
     cannot appear, file, or take a contingent commission in Belgium until
     he is forty-six.
  2. The claim book leaves the building — physically, in a crate, with a
     Commission seal on it. Sixty claims. He signs the transfer receipt and
     the escrow officer counts the folios in the front office.
  3. **The index stays.** Eleven drawers and a laptop, clause 14, personal
     property. Nobody from the Commission so much as asks about it, because
     nobody outside this house has ever understood that the two things are
     different.
  4. Kasimir resigns, because there is nothing left to move. No reproach in
     either direction. He takes the exercise book with him.
  5. The name comes off the door — a sign-writer, two hours, and the ghost
     of the lettering stays in the brick where the paint kept the soot off.
     He stands in the empty front office at six in the evening and
     discovers that he has slept, that night and for the first time in nine
     years, straight through.
- **Payoffs:** clause 14 and the index/claim-book distinction (ch 2, 12);
  Kasimir (ch 8, 10, 24, 27); the register (ch 2).
- **Character movement:** he has been subtracted from. The house is still
  his. The index is still his.

### Ch 36: "Kloosterstraat, Four Doors Down" — Lena, 1,800 words — **QUIET / AFTERMATH**
- **Location:** Antwerp: a hotel lobby, a secondhand bookshop. Friday 15 May.
- **Beat:** aftermath for everyone who is not a lead.
- **% mark:** 92.1–94.7%
- **Emotional arc:** dutiful → shaken → clear
- **Try-fail:** No, but — she can fix none of it, but she can tell the truth
  to the person owed it.
- **Beats:**
  1. **Ruth Schindler-Wolff**, 88, in person, in an Antwerp hotel lobby with
     a folding cane and no interest in gratitude. She asks about the
     tidemark and whether it can be got out. Lena tells her it can be, and
     that it should not be, and why — and it is the first time she has ever
     said the visible-repair argument out loud to a client.
  2. Lena tells her the truth about the 1948 Basel restoration and the
     claim's record. Ruth already suspected. She is eighty-eight and has
     been suspecting things since 1943.
  3. **Tomas Beke**, selling secondhand books four doors from Kloosterstraat.
     Charges dropped in April; accreditation not restored, because
     accreditation is administrative and does not follow an acquittal. He is
     civil to her and does not forgive her and does not need to. **Nobody
     fixes this. It is not fixed by the end of the book.**
  4. She walks past number 118 and looks at the ghost of the lettering in
     the brick and does not go in.
  5. Rachida, by telephone: Article 19 remains available to the Commission
     with respect to Armand Brassart's work, and she is not going to use it,
     and she will not put that in writing, and Lena will have to live with
     an assurance that has no document behind it. For a woman who believes
     only in date-stamps, this is the hardest gift in the book.
- **Payoffs:** Ruth (ch 2, 26); Beke (ch 10, 11); Article 19 (ch 5); the
  tidemark (ch 3).

### Ch 37: "Faller" — Sebastiaan, 2,200 words
- **Location:** the empty front office; a solicitor's letter; Ghent. Tue 19 May.
- **Beat:** the outstanding matters resolve on their own calendars.
- **% mark:** 94.7–97.4%
- **Emotional arc:** indifferent → surprised → still
- **Try-fail:** Yes, and — everything outstanding resolves *and* none of it
  is his doing, which he says out loud to Hanne and she does not care.
- **Beats:**
  1. **The Faller matter.** Nine years in a Zurich tribunal. The award lands
     on the tribunal's own calendar on 19 May: €6.2 million to the
     Corvelijn escrow account as third-party claimant. Nobody in this book
     accelerated it, delayed it, or influenced it, and it was a standing
     joke in a cordage yard in January.
  2. Under the escrow terms the fund is administered by the Commission, not
     by him. Rachida's office directs the first tranche to the twenty-two
     Brassart-authenticated restitutions and to the four claims resting on
     Lucien's nine instruments. The families are made whole from a fund he
     does not control and did not fill.
  3. **Hanne Vandewiele**, executing her father's estate, writes the €4.1m
     off against the escrowed book at a valuation that suits probate. She
     says it is not a gesture, twice, and means it. The second schedule
     Emiel wrote in 2016 passed the controlling vote to the estate, which is
     why she can.
  4. **The Schindler-Wolff estate declines to press the criminal referral.**
     Ruth's instruction, one line, through her Basel lawyer: she has her
     drawing and its true record and she is eighty-eight. Without a
     complainant with standing, the *parket* files it.
  5. He sits in an empty front office with a laptop and eleven drawers and
     takes a call from a museum in Ghent that wants provenance research —
     research, not representation, which the five-year bar does not touch —
     and says yes.
- **Payoffs:** the Faller matter (ch 8); the second schedule (ch 8, 29); the
  nine instruments (ch 31); Ruth (ch 36); the bar's precise scope (ch 35).
- **MICE:** I-thread closes — the Zurich file now carries a true record.

### Ch 38: "Three Times Magnification" — Lena, 2,200 words
- **Location:** Studio 4B; the empty front office at Kloosterstraat.
  Thursday 21 May.
- **Beat:** **Resolution — HFN. She is free to leave and chooses otherwise.**
- **% mark:** 97.4–100%
- **Emotional arc:** deliberate → open
- **Try-fail:** Yes, and — she gets the thing she wants, and it is smaller
  and truer than the thing she wanted in January.
- **Beats:**
  1. **19 May: her 4B key is returned.** The room is the same. The
     fellowship is gone; the board met on 2 May and will not meet again
     until next year, and next year's fragment will be somebody else's.
  2. She works forty minutes on a different object and puts her hand flat on
     the table first, and the tremor is there, and she does the visible fill
     instead of the invisible one, and signs the treatment record.
  3. Her choice is genuinely open and the book makes it explicit: the
     Rotterdam bench is held for her, she has no legal tie to Antwerp, no
     debt, no injunction, no leverage on her, and Armand has told her to
     go.
  4. She goes to 118 and finds an empty front office, eleven drawers, and a
     man with no title, no register entry, no claim book and no staff. He
     asks a direct question and waits for the answer: "Do you want to stay.
     That's the question. I'm not going to build a room around it."
  5. Her answer: "I'm not staying because you gave something up. I'm
     staying because I want to and those aren't the same, and you're going
     to have to live with that being the reason." **Final image:** her
     hands under a lamp at three times magnification, unsteady, working
     anyway, on a fill she has tinted so it can be found — mirroring the
     opening image exactly and inverting it.
- **Payoffs:** the opening image (ch 1); 4B (ch 1, 7, 15, 27); the visible
  repair (ch 32); the fellowship (ch 1, 15, 28, 34).
- **MICE:** M-thread closes.
- **Contract check:** both alive, both present on the page, both choosing.
  HFN, not HEA — nineteen weeks is not long enough for HEA and the book does
  not pretend otherwise. She has a reprimand on her record, a hand that will
  not steady, and no fellowship. He has no register entry until he is
  forty-six.

## Try-fail distribution

| Type | Chapters | Count |
|---|---|---|
| **No, and** | 2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 16, 20, 24, 25, 27, 28, 31 | 12 |
| **Yes, but** | 3, 6, 9, 12, 13, 17, 19, 21, 32, 34 | 10 |
| **Yes, and** | 4, 14, 22, 23, 29, 33, 37, 38 | 8 |
| **No, but** | 1, 7, 15, 18, 26, 30, 35, 36 | 8 |

Thirty-eight chapters, each with exactly one type.

Across the middle (chapters 8–31, twenty-four chapters), ten are "No, and"
and six are "Yes, but" — sixteen of twenty-four, or **67%**, in the two
types that make things harder. Every "Yes, and" in the first three phases is
a win for the darker lead that costs the book something: chapter 4 is the
forgery landing, chapter 14 is him getting the intimacy and keeping the
collateral, chapters 22 and 23 are two people each getting what they wanted
and detonating the same audit. The only chapters that resolve cleanly upward
are 37 and 38.

## Quiet chapters

Ch 15, ch 28, ch 32, ch 36. Two of them are in the back half (32, 36), and
ch 28 and ch 36 are aftermath chapters whose whole business is consequence
rather than escalation. Ch 26 is also aftermath in substance though it sits
inside the retreat.

## Genre contract check against this outline

- **HEA/HFN, both alive, both present, both choosing on the page:** ch 38.
- **The darker lead's own change, demonstrated by a cost paid on the page
  before the resolution:** ch 33 (86.8%) — the corrigendum, the clause 9
  resignation, the claim book into escrow; ch 35 — the five-year bar and
  the name off the door.
- **The hold ended by a decision, not an external event:** ch 33, Tuesday 5
  May, by Sebastiaan filing the corrigendum. Emiel Vandewiele dies on Friday
  8 May, three days later, and the Faller award lands on 19 May. Neither
  frees her and the sequence is fixed in canon precisely so that this cannot
  drift in drafting.
- **The darkness depicted as darkness:** ch 11 (Beke's partner and the
  chain on the door), ch 25 (the body, in full), ch 28 (the diagnosis), ch
  31 (Rachida's line), ch 36 (Beke unrestored). No narration anywhere tells
  the reader how to feel.
- **Negotiated fantasy legible on the page:** ch 19 — terms, limits, the
  word "Basel", and an afterward in which both parties say what it was.
- **Both leads established as adults early and once:** ch 1 (Lena, 33, ten
  years on the register, divorced at 29, lease in her own name) and ch 2
  (Sebastiaan, 41, divorced 2018, nine years running the firm).

Thirty-five threads. Every one has a payoff chapter. Minimum plant-to-payoff
distance is three chapters (#19: planted 14, paid 20 — six; the shortest is
#22, planted 17 and paid 29, twelve; #35 is planted 35 and paid 36, and is
the single deliberate exception, a one-chapter symbolic echo that closes at
38).

### Ledger rules check

- **The protagonists' lies are confronted and resolved on the ledger.**
  Lena's lie (*an invisible repair is not a lie*) is reinforced by #33 in
  chapters 1, 3 and 15, deepened to its worst point by #3 and #22 in chapter
  17, challenged by #28 in chapter 13 and by #27 in chapter 21, and broken
  in chapter 32 where she chooses the visible repair and signs a true record.
  Sebastiaan's lie (*nothing filed can be unfiled*) is stated in chapter 2,
  operationalised in chapter 4, defended in chapter 12, proved horribly
  correct in chapter 31 (#25 — nine instruments, none ever withdrawn), and
  broken in chapter 33 by #1 and #2 together.
- **The climax uses only established mechanisms.** The corrigendum is
  explained in chapter 7 at 17% and again in chapter 31; clause 9 is quoted
  in full in chapter 12 and read back by a second character in chapter 16;
  Article 11 is stated in chapter 2 and chapter 5. Nothing in chapters 33–38
  is a new rule.
- **The irreversible costs are not walked back.** Lena's tremor (#5) is
  permanent and is used in chapters 34, 36 and 38 with no improvement. The
  fellowship (#34) is gone. Tomas Beke (#18) is not restored. Armand's
  exposure under Article 19 (#27) is not extinguished, only unused, and
  without a document. Bram Six is never exposed.
- **Final image mirrors the opening image and shows transformation.** #33
  and #5 together: chapter 1 is steady hands making a loss invisible;
  chapter 38 is unsteady hands making a loss findable.
- **A quiet chapter appears in the back half:** chapters 32 and 36.
